assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector and opened neutrino astronomy with the 2013 discovery of a diffuse astrophysical flux and the 2017 to 2018 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056. This is a new observational window built by instrument builders, which is the kind of achievement I value most.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was central to the detector and the discovery analysis. The credited pair is clean, although the contributions of the wider collaboration and of AMANDA-era colleagues and the Baikal and ANTARES efforts are acknowledged.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established (well above 5 sigma) and the Galactic plane and NGC 1068 results from 2022 to 2023 add independent evidence. The source-identification picture is still developing, but the discovery of the flux itself is mature enough.
uncertainties: I am relying on my recollection of the significance of the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 results rather than a verification.
Whether the prize should instead be shared with others who pioneered the concept, such as early DUMAND proposers, is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, a leap in precision measurement that enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is a clear and lasting instrumental breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the clock; Ye drove it to record accuracy and stability. The two names fit a fair prize, though the prize configuration would need to be balanced against Hall and Hansch in 2005 and Wineland in 2012 and others such as Pierre Lemonde and Hidetoshi Katori's collaborators.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have confirmed performance and the technology is moving toward the redefinition of the SI second. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion clocks could make the committee judge the advance incremental.
I cannot verify the latest accuracy records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, theory by Kane and Mele and the experimental observation in HgTe by Molenkamp's group, created a new class of materials with protected edge and surface states and have had very wide influence. I defer partly to colleagues in condensed matter, but the experimental confirmation by several techniques is convincing even to me.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) made the decisive theoretical predictions, and Molenkamp realised the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells. This candidate list omits Mele and Hasan, so the credit here is narrower than in the related candidate B018. Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work is a separate experimental milestone; I propose two names to keep the credit focused.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations by transport, ARPES and other probes across many materials; the field is mature and the interpretation stable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Hasan and Molenkamp is contested and I cannot resolve it here.
My expertise in this area is limited and I would rely on expert reviewers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers (LCLS, European XFEL, SACLA) made femtosecond, coherent, ultra-bright X-ray pulses a reality and transformed structural biology, chemistry and matter under extreme conditions. It is a landmark accelerator and detector achievement with a large user community.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini was a key originator of the SASE FEL concept and the LCLS effort, and Kim contributed fundamental theory. The credit is spread over many accelerator physicists (including Rossbach, Madey, Bonifacio and others) and I am uncertain who is decisive.
assessment.maturity: The machines operate worldwide and have produced thousands of independent results. The technology is mature.
uncertainties: The Nobel committee may see this as more accelerator engineering than a discovery in physics.
Credit among SASE pioneers is unresolved and I am not certain of the historical details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced precision full-sky maps of the cosmic microwave background and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model, including age, geometry and composition, to percent level. It is a major instrumental and scientific achievement.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument builder and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The credit is well-defined for a mission prize, although it may be thought that COBE and Planck cover related ground.
assessment.maturity: Results are confirmed independently and extended by Planck and ground-based experiments. Recognition would be timely if somewhat late.
uncertainties: Previous prizes for CMB (2006) and for cosmology (2011, 2019) may reduce the appetite for another cosmology award.
A large collaboration makes a three-person limit arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays by NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and CPTA is a remarkable result achieved through decades of patient timing and calibration. It opens the gravitational-wave spectrum below the LIGO band.
assessment.attribution: The credited names represent three different arrays and decades of pulsar-timing development, but the decisive contributions of each are difficult to separate and no single individual is clearly pivotal.
assessment.maturity: The Hellings-Downs signal is at about 3 to 4 sigma in individual arrays; a confident detection and source identification (supermassive black-hole binaries or cosmology) is not yet reached. It may be premature.
uncertainties: The astrophysical origin of the signal is not settled.
The significance may be strengthened by IPTA combined data that I have not seen.
Credit across the arrays is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states created the field of twistronics and a very active new platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery (with Cao and collaborators). This division supports a fair three-person prize, but the contributions of Cao and others are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the key results, but the nature of the superconductivity is still debated and the discovery is only about eight years old.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
The sample dependence of the results is a concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed trapped-ion quantum gates and Blatt's group demonstrated them and built leading ion-trap processors, which has been foundational for quantum computing. The physics is important and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Theory (Cirac and Zoller) and experiment (Blatt) together make a natural trio, although Wineland, Monroe and others share experimental credit and Wineland already has a prize.
assessment.maturity: The scheme has been implemented by many independent groups and commercial machines exist. Maturity is high, but the quantum-information area may be recognised in a broader way in the future.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with candidate B047 which has the same names.
I rely on colleagues for quantum-information judgements.
